boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase campus activities and spaces documented as free for Merrimack students or free to play.

cards.title: Take a Group Fitness Class
cards.subtitle: Sakowich Campus Center
cards.notes: Bring a friend to a 45-minute class such as Pilates, Strength Circuit, restorative yoga or Spin; choose a session that fits both schedules.
cards.short_summary: Instructor-led movement classes for students at every fitness level.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack says its group fitness classes are free for students and include Pilates, Strength Circuit, Restorative Yoga and Spin.
cards.access_notes: Available to students; check the current class offerings before going.

cards.title: Sign Up for Intramural Badminton
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation
cards.notes: Register through IMLeagues, then use badminton as an easy low-stakes way to make a plan with classmates during an intramural session.
cards.short_summary: A free, organized campus sport option listed by Merrimack Recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack lists badminton among its intramural options and states that intramural sports are free to play with IMLeagues sign-up.
cards.access_notes: For students; sports vary by season and require IMLeagues registration.

cards.title: Join Intramural Cornhole
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation
cards.notes: Make a team plan or register individually through IMLeagues when cornhole is offered; confirm the active session and game time first.
cards.short_summary: A casual intramural activity with no play fee.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack lists cornhole among intramural options and states that intramural sports are free to play with IMLeagues sign-up.
cards.access_notes: For students; sports vary by season and require IMLeagues registration.

cards.title: Work Out at Sak Fitness
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Sakowich Campus Center
cards.notes: Meet up for a cardio or strength session, then use the surrounding recreation complex to cool down or continue the hang.
cards.short_summary: A named campus fitness center with student access.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack states that students have free use of all fitness facilities with a valid Merrimack ID; Sakowich Fitness Center is one of those facilities.
cards.access_notes: Valid Merrimack ID required; confirm current facility hours before visiting.

cards.title: Meet at 47 Fitness
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Deegan West Hall
cards.notes: Pair up for a quick cardio or strength workout in the first-year quad, using the open floor space to keep the visit flexible.
cards.short_summary: A named Merrimack fitness center in Deegan West Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack states that students have free use of all fitness facilities with a valid Merrimack ID; 47 Fitness Center is a Merrimack fitness facility.
cards.access_notes: Valid Merrimack ID required; confirm current facility hours before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Indoor Suspended Track
cards.subtitle: Sakowich Recreation Complex
cards.notes: Set an easy lap count and catch up while walking or warming up above the gym floor; it works well before a class or workout.
cards.short_summary: An indoor track in the Sakowich Recreation Complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack identifies an indoor jogging/walking track in the Sakowich Recreation Complex and says students have free use of all fitness facilities with a valid ID.
cards.access_notes: Valid Merrimack ID required; confirm current facility hours before visiting.

cards.title: Catch Open Gym in the MPR
cards.subtitle: Sakowich Recreation Complex
cards.notes: Check whether open gym is running, then bring friends for the basketball, volleyball or pickleball activity scheduled in the multi-purpose room.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus recreation room used for open gym and intramurals.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack says the MPR hosts basketball, volleyball and pickleball, along with open gym time; students have free use of fitness facilities with valid ID.
cards.access_notes: Valid Merrimack ID required; open-gym availability depends on the recreation schedule.

cards.title: Visit the Community Garden
cards.subtitle: Rock Ridge Road
cards.notes: Walk over with friends to see what is growing and, when produce is available, take only what you can use from the community garden.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden with free produce when available.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack reported that the Community Garden’s homegrown fruits and vegetables are available for free to anyone who visits.
cards.source_title: Merrimack’s Best-Kept Secret Offers Fruits, Veggies and Peace of Mind
cards.access_notes: Located next to the house on Rock Ridge Road; availability of produce is seasonal.

cards.title: Play in the Esports Section
cards.subtitle: Student Union, lower level of the Collegiate Church
cards.notes: Bring a small group for the PCs, Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch or Oculus VR; no reservation is needed according to the Student Union FAQ.
cards.short_summary: A 950-square-foot Student Union game room with free play.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack states that esports are free to play and require no reservation; the section includes PCs, Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch and Oculus VR.
cards.access_notes: Use during Student Union operating hours; no reservation is required.

cards.title: Try the Golf Simulator
cards.subtitle: Student Union, lower level of the Collegiate Church
cards.notes: Use the simulator for a low-key group activity, then leave time for setup and play within the Student Union’s posted golf-simulator hours.
cards.short_summary: A free-to-play golf simulator in Merrimack’s Student Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Merrimack’s Student Union FAQ states that golf is free to play and no reservation is required.
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required; the listed simulator hours are 4:30-11 p.m. weekdays and 10 a.m.-11 p.m. weekends, subject to change.
